pairs.subject: proof-carrying-agent-actions
pairs.evidence: apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/modules/book/ProofCheck.tsx:38 When a proof file is labelled with the first format, the checker skips every newer check (applies:false, based only on the file's own format field). The view then shows its green ok chip, 'Every check that applies passed', and proofV2.test.tsx:63-67 locks that in as expected behaviour. So someone holding the owner key could remove the newer records (shield, one_request, owner_saw), relabel the file as v1, re-sign it, and still be shown a pass instead of an inconclusive result.

techniques.evidence: apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/modules/book/ProofCheck.tsx:38 The version floor comes from the file's own label: crates/table-verify/src/v2.rs:21 sets applies:false on every v2 check when bundle.format == PROOF_FORMAT_V1. The view shows that result green, and proofV2.test.tsx:67 asserts PROOF_ALL_THAT_APPLY for an older file. This is the format-downgrade failure the technique names.

apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/modules/book/ProofCheck.tsx:61 Each check's wording comes from the wallet's own table and never from the file. The verdict is report.verified, which the checker computes (table-client lib.rs:288 calls report.verified()), not a field read from the file. Values taken from the file are clipped and shown as plain text only.

apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/modules/book/ProofCheck.tsx:32 The view keeps three outcomes apart: verified, failed (only when a check was actually made and is false) and gold 'Not every check could be made'. Each line shows passed, did-not-pass or not-checked, so a not-checked line is never shown as a pass. The empty-set vacuity is in the checker, outside this context (see notes).

apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/modules/book/proofMarket.test.tsx:52 The view's tests include dishonest and incomplete cases: a forged market record, a failed shield check (proofV2.test.tsx:47) and three not-checked reasons, each asserted never to read 'Every check passed'. This covers the display layer only; fixtures for the verifier itself are in the Rust crates.

apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/console/areas/book/Proof.tsx:31 The report is recomputed every time a file is picked and is never stored as a verdict for a later gate to read, so there is no stale verdict to pin. The authority_manifest/same_version shown is the permission version the deal ran under, not a checker-build identity.

apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/console/areas/book/BookLayer.tsx:6 The proofs checked here cover deals (signed transcripts, PayPal order records, audit rows), not agent-authored diffs. No test oracle is part of any proof, so there is nothing to weaken.

pairs.registryProposal: The subject is written for agent code changes and merge gates, but the same shape fits a signed per-action proof file (here, a payment deal) that a person checks offline with a deterministic checker. The format-downgrade rule in proof-class-bound-to-action-class carries over directly. A short note that the subject also covers signed action records with no merge gate, and that a viewer must not render a lighter older-format verdict in the same 'passed' tone, would help.
